name: on-exception mode, both reopens spent — the escalation stop finally fires
why: The two stops no other walk reaches. VERDICT declares `escalation`, which is silent while reopens remain — every other fixture leaves VERDICT without stopping, and this one asserts that it DOES stop once attempts.QA reaches its bound. on-exception mode is asserted alongside it: two gates are skipped for host:none and the run must stop at each, because the ledger's design is record-and-continue and this mode exists to stop that meaning 'find out at DONE'. Resumed mid-run, which is itself the thing the state file is for.

skipped_gates.reason: SIMULATED: carried in from earlier in this run

steps.observation: RESUMED here. Both reopens are already spent — attempts.QA reads 2 — so this pass through the tail is the last one the graph is allowed to take on its own.

host is none: no remote, so no PR to open. Ledgered and passed through — never a halt. Under on-exception mode that ledger entry is itself a stop, which is the point of the mode: record-and-continue is right, but you should not learn at DONE that a gate ran degraded.

skipped_gates.reason: SIMULATED: context.host == none, no remote and therefore no PR to open.

steps.observation: SKIPPED GATE: host is none, so there is no PR to review either. code-review:code-review is ledgered and the node passes straight through — one exit, and it never blocks.

Second ledger entry, second stop. Edge 22a and not 22b — the app IS runnable, so QA is not skipped. Note that auto_open_mr is true, so PR's confirm-before did NOT fire above; the only stop there was the mode's.

steps.observation: A third BLOCK. The app runs and the finding is real, so this is qa.verdict = BLOCK rather than a missing-qa_env BLOCKED — the first spends a reopen, the second would not, and collapsing them would burn the budget on a typo.

steps.observation: THE ESCALATION STOP. Silent while reopens remained — every other walk leaves VERDICT without stopping, correctly — and it fires exactly once, when the bound is spent. The graph does not grant itself a third reopen: bounds are never widened from the inside. tried[] carries the architectural doubt forward so the human inherits the thought instead of losing it.
